evidence.snippet: const s3Client = new S3Client({ region: process.env.AWS_REGION!, credentials: { accessKeyId: process.env.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID!, secretAccessKey: process.env.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY! } });
evidence.why: Secret AWS credentials are read and an S3Client constructed at module top-level scope, with no server-only guard.
This client component imports from lib/s3Upload.ts, pulling the module (and its top-level S3Client/secret construction side effect) into the client bundle.

Importing the shared module causes the secret-reading S3Client instantiation code to execute on module load in the browser bundle, since there is no server-only separation (e.g. 'server-only' package or split file).

controls_present: presigned URL pattern keeps actual upload request from needing credentials
server route handlers perform privileged S3 calls
other_classes_observed: mixing server-only secret-using module with client-imported module without 'server-only' guard (architecture risk)
